task: Compared alternate lineations of one passage, redrafted a poem under exact syllable and stanza limits, and composed then rescanned an alliterative address.
observations: Rebreaking unchanged syntax produced distinct closure, forward pull, and temporary emphasis that could be compared independently of diction.
An exact syllable container exposed forced enjambments and awkward syntax while also generating usable alternative phrasing.
Visible initial-letter matches did not consistently create audible alliteration until lexical stress, contextual emphasis, and spacing between beats were rescanned.
notes: The exercises completed their target operations in one session. Retention and transfer were not tested, so no compact memory conclusion is warranted.

task: Built a counterbalanced word inventory, retold one incident through two idiolects, drafted and revised a nonhuman persona, expanded then compressed an unusual incident, and ran applicable title, lineation, stress, alliterative-address, and deliberately-generic-persona reversal drills.
observations: The witness version became more distinct when noticed details, evaluation, and social permission changed; decorative speech markers alone did not create a different voice.
The nonhuman persona strengthened when observable properties, affordances, desire, syntax, and sound interacted, while an obvious verbal gimmick flattened the speaker.
Removing explicit motive preserved mystery only where actions, objects, sequence, and consequences still supported inference.
A favorite-word inventory exposed recurring affinities but one session could not establish a stable or transferable authorial voice.
notes: The multi-occasion cross-discourse progression was not completed; one bounded pass was performed and is not treated as retention or transfer evidence.

task: Applied applicable imagery, comparison, voice, lineation, rhythm, sound, title, revision, concrete-word, and concise-observation drills while reading and responding to several poems and object-imagery exercises.
observations: Image sequences gained rhetorical force when scale, recurrence, and return were arranged deliberately rather than ranked only from weak to strong.
Transferring a comparison exposed the concrete property that made the original bridge work and separated productive strangeness from random absurdity.
A locally mysterious image remained effective when emotional sequence, sound, and consequence supported it; unexplained novelty without those relations collapsed during revision.
Literalizing a received phrase could recover its dormant objects and actions, but recognition alone did not restore force.
Visual inspection showed that lineation and stanza shape paced image disclosure and could not be recovered reliably from flattened extraction alone.
notes: Daily-haiku and multi-session cull cycles received only bounded first-session work and do not count as retention tests. Form mapping lacked three examples of one inherited form, and cento construction was not run because reuse permission was not established.
